question.problem: In a right triangle $△FGH,$ $∠H$ is a right angle, $FH=2\sqrt{2}$ and $FG=6.$ Find the cosine of $∠G.$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/e585e89d11dea316c5483eeb2b2fc4750084409651ecf838e65a0d09e7bcc97f.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡G=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{GH}{FG}=\frac{GH}{6}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing length $GH.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}GH & =\sqrt{F{G}^{2}-F{H}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}-(2\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36-8} \\  & =\sqrt{28} \\  & =2\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡G & =\frac{GH}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{7}}{6} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
